source.title: Holiday calendars written for Prospero Dungeon
source.note: Public holidays and observances from general knowledge. Moved weekend dates ("observed" and substitute days) are not included. Korean lunar holidays follow KASI tables and Japan's equinox days the almanac formula, for 2024-2040.

holidays.name: New Year's Day
holidays.summary: A slow day after the night before; most things closed.

holidays.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Day
holidays.summary: Federal holiday with days of service and marches; schools and government offices close.

holidays.name: Valentine's Day
holidays.summary: Restaurants book up; cards and flowers.

holidays.name: Presidents' Day
holidays.summary: Federal holiday; government offices and many schools close, and stores run sales.

holidays.name: St. Patrick's Day
holidays.summary: Green beer, parades and crowded pubs.

holidays.name: Easter Sunday
holidays.summary: Church services, egg hunts and family brunch.

holidays.name: Mother's Day
holidays.summary: Brunch reservations and calls home.

holidays.name: Memorial Day
holidays.summary: The unofficial start of summer: cookouts, beaches and remembrance of the war dead.

holidays.name: Father's Day
holidays.summary: Cookouts and calls home.

holidays.name: Juneteenth
holidays.summary: Marks the end of slavery in the United States; festivals and cookouts.

holidays.name: Independence Day
holidays.summary: Fireworks, cookouts and a day off.

holidays.name: Labor Day
holidays.summary: The unofficial end of summer and a long weekend.

holidays.name: Halloween
holidays.summary: Costumes, trick-or-treating and parties.

holidays.name: Veterans Day
holidays.summary: Federal holiday; government offices and banks close.

holidays.name: Thanksgiving
holidays.summary: A big family meal, football and travel; most things close.

holidays.name: Christmas Eve
holidays.summary: Last-minute shopping and family gatherings; many offices close early.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.summary: Presents and family; almost everything closes.

holidays.name: New Year's Eve
holidays.summary: Parties and countdowns at midnight.

holidays.name: New Year's Day
holidays.summary: A bank holiday: a slow, hungover day, a walk and the football.

holidays.name: Valentine's Day
holidays.summary: Restaurants book up; cards, roses and set menus.

holidays.name: Pancake Day (Shrove Tuesday)
holidays.summary: Pancakes with lemon and sugar, and pancake races in some towns.

holidays.name: Mothering Sunday
holidays.summary: Flowers, cards and Sunday lunch out with mum; pubs and restaurants are full.

holidays.name: St Patrick's Day
holidays.summary: Guinness, parades and crowded Irish pubs.

holidays.name: Good Friday
holidays.summary: A bank holiday: hot cross buns and the start of a four-day weekend.

holidays.name: Easter Sunday
holidays.summary: Chocolate eggs, egg hunts, church for some and a roast lunch.

holidays.name: Easter Monday
holidays.summary: A bank holiday in England and Wales: garden centres, DIY and day trips.

holidays.name: St George's Day
holidays.summary: England's saint's day: a few flags and the odd pub event, and an ordinary working day.

holidays.name: Early May bank holiday
holidays.summary: A long weekend: May Day fairs, morris dancing and the first barbecues.

holidays.name: Spring bank holiday
holidays.summary: A long weekend at the end of May: traffic to the coast and half-term for schools.

holidays.name: Father's Day
holidays.summary: Cards, a pub lunch and socks.

holidays.name: Summer bank holiday
holidays.summary: The last long weekend of summer in England and Wales: festivals, Notting Hill Carnival in London and packed beaches.

holidays.name: Halloween
holidays.summary: Costumes, trick-or-treating and fancy-dress parties.

holidays.name: Bonfire Night
holidays.summary: Guy Fawkes Night: bonfires, fireworks displays in the parks, sparklers and toffee apples.

holidays.name: Armistice Day
holidays.summary: Two minutes' silence at 11 a.m. and poppies on coats.

holidays.name: Remembrance Sunday
holidays.summary: Wreaths laid at the Cenotaph and war memorials, and two minutes' silence at eleven.

holidays.name: Christmas Eve
holidays.summary: Last-minute shopping, the pub with friends from home and midnight Mass.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.summary: Presents, crackers, turkey, the King's speech at three and almost everything shut, trains included.

holidays.name: Boxing Day
holidays.summary: A bank holiday: leftovers, the sales, football and a long walk.

holidays.name: New Year's Eve
holidays.summary: Parties, the fireworks over the river at midnight and Auld Lang Syne.

holidays.name: New Year's Day
holidays.summary: Sinjeong: watching the first sunrise of the year from a beach or peak, and tteokguk.

holidays.name: Seollal holiday
holidays.summary: The day before Lunar New Year: the great traffic jam out of the cities and cooking jeon at home.

holidays.name: Seollal (Lunar New Year)
holidays.summary: Ancestral rites, tteokguk, deep bows to elders for sebae money and games of yut; most shops close.

holidays.name: Seollal holiday
holidays.summary: The last day of the New Year holiday: visiting the other side of the family and the drive home.

holidays.name: Valentine's Day
holidays.summary: Women give men chocolate; cafes and convenience stores are stacked with gift boxes.

holidays.name: Samiljeol (Independence Movement Day)
holidays.summary: Marks the 1919 independence protests: flags on balconies and ceremonies.

holidays.name: White Day
holidays.summary: Men return the favour with candy, flowers and dinner.

holidays.name: Black Day
holidays.summary: Singles without a valentine meet for black-bean jajangmyeon, half joking.

holidays.name: Workers' Day
holidays.summary: Many companies give the day off; schools and government offices stay open.

holidays.name: Children's Day
holidays.summary: Parks, zoos and amusement parks packed with families; presents for the kids.

holidays.name: Parents' Day
holidays.summary: Red carnations pinned on parents, a meal out and an envelope of money.

holidays.name: Buddha's Birthday
holidays.summary: Lanterns strung through temple courtyards and the streets; free temple bibimbap.

holidays.name: Teachers' Day
holidays.summary: Students thank teachers with carnations and letters.

holidays.name: Memorial Day
holidays.summary: Hyeonchungil: a siren at 10 a.m. and a minute of silence for the war dead; flags at half-mast.

holidays.name: Constitution Day
holidays.summary: Jeheonjeol, marking the 1948 constitution: flags out, ceremonies.

holidays.name: Liberation Day
holidays.summary: Gwangbokjeol, the end of Japanese rule in 1945: flags, ceremonies and bells.

holidays.name: Chuseok holiday
holidays.summary: The day before Chuseok: the exodus to hometowns, and songpyeon made together.

holidays.name: Chuseok
holidays.summary: The harvest moon festival: ancestral rites, tending family graves, songpyeon and family gift sets.

holidays.name: Chuseok holiday
holidays.summary: The last day of the Chuseok holiday and the long drive back.

holidays.name: Gaecheonjeol (National Foundation Day)
holidays.summary: The legendary founding of Gojoseon by Dangun; a quiet day off.

holidays.name: Hangul Day
holidays.summary: Celebrates the Korean alphabet: exhibitions and a day off.

holidays.name: Halloween
holidays.summary: Costume parties in the clubbing districts.

holidays.name: Pepero Day
holidays.summary: Boxes of chocolate-dipped Pepero sticks traded between friends and couples.

holidays.name: Christmas Eve
holidays.summary: A couples' night: booked-out restaurants, cakes and lit-up streets.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.summary: A day off spent as a couple or with friends more than family; church for some.

holidays.name: New Year's Eve
holidays.summary: The Bosingak bell rung at midnight, and countdowns.

holidays.name: New Year's Day
holidays.summary: Ganjitsu: the first shrine visit, osechi boxes, nengajo cards in the post and offices shut.

holidays.name: New Year holiday
holidays.summary: Offices and banks stay shut; department stores open with fukubukuro lucky bags.

holidays.name: New Year holiday
holidays.summary: The last day of the New Year break: Hakone Ekiden on TV and the trip back to the city.

holidays.name: Coming of Age Day
holidays.summary: Twenty-year-olds in furisode and suits at city ceremonies, then out drinking.

holidays.name: Setsubun
holidays.summary: Beans thrown to drive out demons and an ehomaki roll eaten in silence facing the lucky direction.

holidays.name: National Foundation Day
holidays.summary: Kenkoku Kinen no Hi: a quiet day off.

holidays.name: Valentine's Day
holidays.summary: Women give chocolate: honmei for a crush, giri for coworkers.

holidays.name: Emperor's Birthday
holidays.summary: A day off; the palace opens for the Emperor's greeting.

holidays.name: Hinamatsuri
holidays.summary: Girls' Day: tiered doll displays, chirashi sushi and pink amazake.

holidays.name: White Day
holidays.summary: A month after Valentine's, men return gifts, supposedly three times the value.

holidays.name: Vernal Equinox Day
holidays.summary: Shunbun no Hi: family graves visited for higan, and the first cherry blossom forecasts.

holidays.name: Showa Day
holidays.summary: Golden Week begins: trains and airports fill.

holidays.name: Constitution Memorial Day
holidays.summary: Golden Week: crowded resorts, festivals and queues everywhere.

holidays.name: Greenery Day
holidays.summary: Golden Week: parks and gardens full.

holidays.name: Children's Day
holidays.summary: The end of Golden Week: koinobori carp streamers and kashiwa mochi.

holidays.name: Tanabata
holidays.summary: Wishes written on paper strips hung on bamboo, for the star-crossed lovers.

holidays.name: Marine Day
holidays.summary: Umi no Hi: the beaches open and summer starts in earnest.

holidays.name: Mountain Day
holidays.summary: Yama no Hi: a day off at the start of the Obon season.

holidays.name: Obon
holidays.summary: Ancestors welcomed home for four days: trips to hometowns, bon odori dances and lanterns; many businesses close for the week.

holidays.name: Respect for the Aged Day
holidays.summary: Keiro no Hi: visits and gifts for grandparents.

holidays.name: Citizens' Holiday
holidays.summary: A day off sandwiched between two holidays, making a five-day Silver Week.

holidays.name: Autumnal Equinox Day
holidays.summary: Shubun no Hi: graves tended for autumn higan and ohagi rice cakes.

holidays.name: Sports Day
holidays.summary: Supotsu no Hi: school and neighbourhood sports days, relays and tug-of-war.

holidays.name: Halloween
holidays.summary: Costumed crowds in the nightlife districts and on the trains.

holidays.name: Culture Day
holidays.summary: Bunka no Hi: museums, school culture festivals and awards.

holidays.name: Shichi-Go-San
holidays.summary: Children of three, five and seven dressed up for shrine visits and photos, with chitose-ame candy.

holidays.name: Labour Thanksgiving Day
holidays.summary: Kinro Kansha no Hi: a day off and the first year-end parties.

holidays.name: Christmas Eve
holidays.summary: The date night of the year: illuminations, booked restaurants, Christmas cake and fried chicken.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.summary: An ordinary working day; the decorations come down for the New Year pine.

holidays.name: New Year's Eve
holidays.summary: Omisoka: offices shut from the 29th, toshikoshi soba, Kohaku on TV and temple bells rung 108 times at midnight.

holidays.name: New Year's Day
holidays.summary: Hangovers from the night before, calls on family and a quiet city until noon.

holidays.name: Lincoln's Birthday
holidays.summary: A legal holiday in New York and much of the North: banks and schools close there, flags fly and veterans of the Union march.

holidays.name: Valentine's Day
holidays.summary: Penny cards and lace valentines, boxes of chocolates and a dance or two.

holidays.name: Washington's Birthday
holidays.summary: Banks, offices and schools close; cherry pie, store sales and patriotic speeches.

holidays.name: St. Patrick's Day
holidays.summary: The parade up Fifth Avenue and green carnations, with Prohibition doing little to keep anyone dry.

holidays.name: Easter Sunday
holidays.summary: Church in new spring hats, then the Easter Parade along the avenue to see and be seen.

holidays.name: Mother's Day
holidays.summary: A white carnation worn for mother, a card home and Sunday dinner.

holidays.name: Decoration Day
holidays.summary: Graves decorated with flowers and flags for the dead of the Civil War and the Great War; parades, then the first trips to the shore.

holidays.name: Independence Day
holidays.summary: Firecrackers, parades, picnics, ball games and packed beaches.

holidays.name: Labor Day
holidays.summary: Union parades and picnics, and the end of straw-hat season.

holidays.name: Columbus Day
holidays.summary: A state holiday in New York, Massachusetts and most of the Northeast; Italian societies march with bands and banners.

holidays.name: Hallowe'en
holidays.summary: Masquerade parties, bobbing for apples, fortune games and boys up to pranks after dark.

holidays.name: Armistice Day
holidays.summary: Two minutes of silence at the eleventh hour, then parades of Great War veterans; a legal holiday in most states.

holidays.name: Thanksgiving Day
holidays.summary: The last Thursday of November: turkey, family, the big college football games and the department-store parade.

holidays.name: Christmas Eve
holidays.summary: Last shopping at the department stores, carols and midnight Mass.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.summary: Church, a tree with electric lights, presents and a big dinner; almost everything closes.

holidays.name: New Year's Eve
holidays.summary: Times Square crowds, noisemakers, hotel ballrooms and speakeasies packed until dawn.

holidays.name: New Year's Day
holidays.summary: Calls on friends and an open house in the parlour.

holidays.name: Washington's Birthday
holidays.summary: Speeches, a ball and a day off for banks and offices.

holidays.name: Easter Sunday
holidays.summary: Church in new clothes and a big dinner after.

holidays.name: Decoration Day
holidays.summary: Veterans and townsfolk decorate soldiers' graves with flowers, with a procession and speeches.

holidays.name: Independence Day
holidays.summary: The biggest day of the year: parade, oration, races, a barbecue and fireworks.

holidays.name: Thanksgiving Day
holidays.summary: Proclaimed each year for the last Thursday of November: church, turkey and a shooting match.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.summary: Church, a tree, presents and a big dinner.

holidays.name: New Year's Day
holidays.summary: Not a holiday in England; Scots keep Hogmanay.

holidays.name: Lady Day
holidays.summary: A quarter day: rents fall due and servants' terms change.

holidays.name: Shrove Tuesday
holidays.summary: Pancake day, with football in some towns.

holidays.name: Good Friday
holidays.summary: Shops shut, hot cross buns and church.

holidays.name: Easter Sunday
holidays.summary: Church and a family dinner.

holidays.name: Easter Monday
holidays.summary: A bank holiday: excursion trains, fairs and Hampstead Heath crowded with day-trippers.

holidays.name: The Queen's Birthday
holidays.summary: Flags, a royal salute and, in the colonies, a holiday.

holidays.name: Whit Monday
holidays.summary: A bank holiday: Whit walks, Sunday-school treats and excursions.

holidays.name: Midsummer Day
holidays.summary: A quarter day when rents fall due.

holidays.name: August Bank Holiday
holidays.summary: The first Monday in August: seaside trips, crowded trains and fairs.

holidays.name: Michaelmas
holidays.summary: A quarter day; goose for dinner and hiring fairs.

holidays.name: Guy Fawkes Night
holidays.summary: Bonfires, guys carried through the streets and fireworks.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.summary: Church, a goose or a joint, plum pudding and family.

holidays.name: Boxing Day
holidays.summary: A bank holiday: Christmas boxes for tradesmen and servants, and the pantomime season opens.

holidays.name: Twelfth Night
holidays.summary: The last night of Christmas: a bean in the cake makes a king for the evening.

holidays.name: Epiphany
holidays.summary: The end of the twelve days of Christmas.

holidays.name: Plough Monday
holidays.summary: Ploughboys drag a decorated plough round the town begging for pennies before work starts again.

holidays.name: Candlemas
holidays.summary: Candles blessed in church and carried in procession.

holidays.name: Shrove Tuesday
holidays.summary: Feasting, cock-throwing and football before Lent.

holidays.name: Ash Wednesday
holidays.summary: Lent begins: no meat until Easter.

holidays.name: Lady Day
holidays.summary: The Annunciation and the start of the year; a quarter day.

holidays.name: Palm Sunday
holidays.summary: Procession with yew and willow for palms.

holidays.name: Good Friday
holidays.summary: Creeping to the cross; a day of fasting.

holidays.name: Easter Day
holidays.summary: Lent ends: meat, eggs and ale, and a day free of work.

holidays.name: Hock Monday
holidays.summary: The women of the town rope the men and let them go for a forfeit; the men return the favour next day.

holidays.name: May Day
holidays.summary: Bringing in the may at dawn, a maypole and dancing.

holidays.name: Ascension Day
holidays.summary: Beating the bounds of the parish.

holidays.name: Whitsunday (Pentecost)
holidays.summary: A great feast; the king holds court and church ales are brewed.

holidays.name: St John's Eve
holidays.summary: Bonfires on the hills and watch fires in the town.

holidays.name: Lammas
holidays.summary: Loaf-mass: bread from the first wheat blessed in church.

holidays.name: Michaelmas
holidays.summary: Rents and reeves' accounts due, and a goose for dinner.

holidays.name: All Hallows
holidays.summary: Bells rung for the dead through the night before.

holidays.name: Martinmas
holidays.summary: Beasts slaughtered and salted for winter; a feast of fresh meat.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.summary: Twelve days of feasting, games and no work in the fields.
